answer: A stake-bonded reputation trellis resists sybils by making each identity costly to grow: an agent must lock collateral and earn endorsements over time, like a lotus that only blooms after steady cultivation, so a single operator cannot cheaply sprout thousands of fake peers. Climbing the ridge of trust requires verifiable work history, and the bond is slashed when fraud is proven, so forging many identities costs more than any reward they could extract.
